description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the number of frames and accuracy (in percent) for four different video understanding methods. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Frames,” spans from approximately 5 to 65 with major tick marks at intervals of 10, using a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy (%)”, ranges from 39 to 55 with major tick marks at intervals of 1, also on a linear scale. Four distinct lines are plotted: “Ours (Dynamic Seg)” (blue with circle markers, solid line) starts at ~53% at 10 frames, rises slightly to ~54% at 15 frames, then remains nearly flat through 65 frames. “Ours (Static 4-Seg)” (green with circle markers, solid line) begins at ~52.5% at 10 frames, increases to ~53.8% at 15 frames, and then plateaus near 54% through 65 frames. “PLLaVA (DP 16)” (red with square markers, solid line) starts at ~45.5% at 15 frames, declines gradually to ~43.8% at 30 frames, and continues to drop slowly to ~42.2% at 65 frames. The fourth line, represented by orange squares and a solid line (labeled in the legend as “PLLaVA (DP 16)” but visually distinct from the red line), begins at ~45% at 10 frames, drops to ~43% at 15 frames, continues declining to ~41% at 30 frames, and reaches ~39.5% at 65 frames. All lines show either a plateau or a downward trend as the number of frames increases, with the two “Ours” methods maintaining the highest and most stable accuracy.
